title: Start Here: What Is Thai?
subtitle: The absolute basics before any letters
summary: Thai is spoken by about 70 million people and written with its own alphabet (not A-Z). It is a tonal language: the pitch of your voice changes a word's meaning. Before learning individual letters, this lesson gives you the big picture so everything later makes sense.
key_takeaways: Thai uses its own alphabet - not the English letters.
Thai is tonal: the same basic sound said at a different pitch can mean a different word.
There are 5 tones: mid, low, falling, high, and rising.
Thai words run together with no spaces - you learn to find the breaks by feel.
The Thai keyboard (Kedmanee) has 44 consonants plus vowels and tone marks.
You do not need to memorise everything now - this app teaches it a little at a time.

title: The Zero-Point Canvas
subtitle: Linear Left-to-Right Anchors & Unaspirated Stops
summary: Your first letters make simple left-to-right sounds. A consonant plus a long vowel like า makes a steady, neutral (mid) tone. You type these letters in the same order you read them, like English.

characters.sound_guide: Unaspirated 'g / k' sound, like 'k' in English 'skill' (never aspirated like 'kill').
characters.lookalike_warning: No head loop! Do not confuse with ภ (outward head) or ถ (inward head).

characters.sound_guide: Silent initial bearer for standalone vowels, or long 'aw' vowel sound.
characters.lookalike_warning: Head loop starts top-left and sweeps down clockwise.

characters.sound_guide: Unaspirated 'j / ch' sound, like 'j' in 'jeep' but crisp.
characters.lookalike_warning: Single smooth downward arch with a small top loop.

characters.sound_guide: Long open 'aa' sound as in 'father'. Sits on the right side of the consonant.
characters.lookalike_warning: Always typed AFTER the base consonant.

key_takeaways: Thai is written left to right, just like English.
ก sounds like a soft 'g/k' with no puff of air (like the 'k' in 'skill').
อ is a silent holder for vowel sounds (and can also be the 'aw' vowel).
จ sounds like a crisp 'j' (like the 'j' in 'jeep').
า is a long 'aa' sound and goes AFTER the consonant (กา = 'gaa').

ตามาหาอา

title: Anatomy of the Head-Loop
subtitle: The Lookalike Code & Visual Anchors
summary: Some Thai letters look almost identical. The trick is the little loop at the top: ด has a smooth rounded top, while ต has a small dent. Similarly, บ and ป have the same body but different tail heights. Slow down and compare the tops.

characters.sound_guide: Standard 'd' sound as in 'dog'.
characters.lookalike_warning: Head loop goes inside and down with a smooth rounded crown. Look out for ต!

characters.sound_guide: Unaspirated 'dt' sound, like 't' in 'stop' (no breath of air).
characters.lookalike_warning: Identical to ด except its crown has a cleft (dented zigzag notch on top).

characters.sound_guide: Standard 'b' sound as in 'boy'.
characters.lookalike_warning: Square base, short vertical tail level with the letter height.

characters.sound_guide: Unaspirated 'bp' sound, like 'p' in 'spin'.
characters.lookalike_warning: Exact same body as บ, but its right tail shoots straight up above the line!

key_takeaways: ด ('d', like 'dog') has a smooth, rounded top.
ต ('dt', like 'stop') looks like ด but has a tiny dent or notch on top.
บ ('b', like 'boy') and ป ('bp', like 'spin') share a body - ป's tail shoots up higher.
When two letters look the same, compare the very top first.

title: The Left-Shift Shock
subtitle: Pre-posed Vowels & Temporal Typing Paradox
summary: Some Thai vowels are written to the LEFT of the consonant, but you say them AFTER it. For example, ไป is 'bpai' - the ใ (ai) comes first in writing but last in speech. On the keyboard you must type the vowel first, then the consonant.

characters.sound_guide: Long 'ay' sound as in 'say' (monophthong).
characters.lookalike_warning: Must be typed BEFORE the consonant (e.g. เท = เ + ท).

characters.sound_guide: Broad 'ae' sound as in English 'cat' or 'bad'.
characters.lookalike_warning: A single key (C), do NOT press เ twice!

characters.sound_guide: Long 'oh' sound as in 'go'. Tall ascender swings above standard height.
characters.lookalike_warning: Lives on the Shift layer (Shift + F).

characters.name_thai: สระ ไอ ไม้มลาย
characters.sound_guide: Diphthong 'ai' as in 'eye' or 'sky'.
characters.lookalike_warning: Has a zigzag crown. Used for general words like ไป (go), ไกล (far).

characters.name_thai: สระ ใอ ไม้ม้วน
characters.sound_guide: Identical 'ai' sound to ไ, but used strictly in exactly 20 special Thai words.
characters.lookalike_warning: Has a curled spiral loop on top. Used in ใน (in), ให้ (give), ใหม่ (new).

key_takeaways: Left-side vowels (เ แ โ ใ ไ) sit before the consonant but are said after it.
To type ไป, press ไ first, then ป.
แ has its own key - never type two เ to make it.
ไ and ใ sound the same 'ai'; ใ is used in only about 20 special words.
Type in the same order you see: vowel first, then consonant.

title: Vertical Stacking
subtitle: The Y-Axis Vowels & Cap Anatomy
summary: Thai vowels can sit above (ิ ี ึ) or below (ุ ู) the consonant. You type the consonant first, then add the vowel on top or bottom. The marks look similar - the difference is a tiny tick or loop on top.

characters.sound_guide: Short 'i' sound as in 'sit'. Sits on top of the consonant.
characters.lookalike_warning: Smooth curved cap with NO vertical stroke.

characters.sound_guide: Long 'ee' sound as in 'see'. Sits on top of the consonant.
characters.lookalike_warning: Curved cap WITH one vertical tick on the top right.

characters.sound_guide: Guttural short 'ue' sound made with teeth closed and tongue pulled back.
characters.lookalike_warning: Curved cap with a small closed circular loop on the top right.

characters.sound_guide: Short 'u' sound as in 'put'. Sits underneath the consonant.
characters.lookalike_warning: Small ribbon loop hanging below the baseline.

characters.sound_guide: Long 'oo' sound as in 'moon'. Sits underneath the consonant.
characters.lookalike_warning: Looks like a miniature บ underneath the letter. Lives on Shift+6.

key_takeaways: Top vowels: ิ (short i), ี (long ee), ึ (short ue).
Bottom vowels: ุ (short u), ู (long oo).
Type the consonant first, then the vowel (ด + ี = ดี).
Look for the small tick (long ee) or loop (ue) on top.
Bottom vowels hang under the letter (ดู = d + oo).

title: The Tone Algebra Engine
subtitle: Live vs. Dead Syllables & Natural Base Tones
summary: Thai tones depend partly on whether a syllable is 'live' (it keeps ringing - ends in a long vowel or in m/n/ng) or 'dead' (it stops short - ends in a p/t/k sound). For mid-class letters: live = mid tone, dead = low tone. You can often predict the tone before seeing any tone mark.

characters.sound_guide: Crisp 'ng' sound as in 'sing', even at the start of a word.
characters.lookalike_warning: Single diagonal slant with an inward loop.

characters.sound_guide: Standard 'n' sound as in 'no'. Creates a Live syllable ending.
characters.lookalike_warning: Bottom loop sits on the right. Compare with ม where the loop is on the left!

characters.sound_guide: Standard 'm' sound as in 'mom'. Creates a Live syllable ending.
characters.lookalike_warning: Bottom loop sits on the left front.

key_takeaways: A 'live' syllable ends in a long vowel or m/n/ng - the sound continues.
A 'dead' syllable ends in a short vowel or a p/t/k stop - it cuts off.
Mid-class letter + live = mid tone (e.g. บิน = bin).
Mid-class letter + dead = low tone (e.g. ปิด = bpit).
You can often predict the tone just from how the syllable ends.

title: The Consonant Class War
subtitle: High Class Rising Tones & Low Class Resonators
summary: Thai consonants come in three 'classes': mid, high, and low. The class changes the tone. High-class letters on an open syllable naturally rise (e.g. ขา = rising). Low-class letters stay mid (e.g. คา = mid). A letter's class matters as much as its sound.

characters.sound_guide: Aspirated 'kh' sound with an inherent rising pitch in live syllables.
characters.lookalike_warning: Narrow body with a clean top loop. Look out for ช (which has a tail)!

characters.sound_guide: Crisp 's' sound as in 'sun'. Inherent rising tone on open syllables.
characters.lookalike_warning: Identical to ล except ส has a small tail flicking off its top right corner!

characters.sound_guide: Standard 'h' sound. Also acts as a silent tone-shifter (ห นำ).
characters.lookalike_warning: Two loops: one at top-left, one at bottom-right.

characters.sound_guide: Aspirated 'kh' sound. Low-class consonant with natural Mid tone on live syllables.
characters.lookalike_warning: Head loop opens outward to the right. Do not confuse with ด!

key_takeaways: Every consonant is one of three classes: mid, high, or low.
High class + live syllable = rising tone (ขา = rising).
Low class + live syllable = mid tone (คา = mid).
ส has a tiny tail on top; ล has none - the easy way to tell them apart.
Class is about tone, not sound - two letters can sound the same but act differently.

title: The 3-Tier Cascade
subtitle: Tone Marks & The Low-Class Multiplier
summary: Two little marks change the tone: ่ (mai ek) and ้ (mai tho). Their effect depends on the consonant class. On mid/high letters, ่ = low tone and ้ = falling tone. On low letters, ่ = falling and ้ = high. Type them in order: consonant, then vowel, then tone mark.

characters.sound_guide: Makes Mid/High consonants Low tone; makes Low consonants Falling tone!
characters.lookalike_warning: Single vertical stroke stacked on Tier 3 (topmost layer).

characters.sound_guide: Makes Mid/High consonants Falling tone; makes Low consonants High tone!
characters.lookalike_warning: Curved zigzag mark stacked on Tier 3.

key_takeaways: Tone marks sit on the top layer, above the consonant and vowel.
Mid/high class + ่ = low tone; + ้ = falling tone.
Low class + ่ = falling tone; + ้ = high tone.
Type in order: consonant, then vowel, then tone mark (ที่ = ท + ี + ่).
The consonant class decides what a tone mark does.

title: The Chameleon Vowels
subtitle: Invisible Zero-Vowels & Mai Han-Akat Mutations
summary: Thai sometimes hides a vowel or changes its shape. Two consonants with no vowel make a short 'o' (คน = khon). A short 'a' turns into a small mark (ั) when a final consonant comes (วัน = wan). And the vowel เ-อ becomes เ-ิ with a final consonant (เดิน = doen).

characters.name_thai: ไม้หันอากาศ
characters.sound_guide: Short 'a' sound as in 'cup' or 'run'. Sits above initial consonant.
characters.lookalike_warning: Single curved crescent above the letter. Replaces ะ when a final consonant is present.

characters.sound_guide: Short abrupt 'a' sound. Follows the consonant immediately.
characters.lookalike_warning: Two small stacked loops on the right side.

key_takeaways: Two consonants with no vowel = a hidden short 'o' (คน, นก).
Short 'a' + final consonant = ั on top (วัน = ว + ั + น).
The vowel เ-อ turns into เ-ิ when a final consonant is added (เดิน).
If you cannot find a vowel key, the vowel may be invisible - just type the consonants.
Listen for the vowel; the spelling may hide it.

title: Clusters & The Silent Killer
subtitle: Consonant Blends, Karan Mark & The Repetition Symbol
summary: Thai can put two consonants together with no vowel (a blend, like ปล- in ปลา). It also has a silent mark ์ that kills a letter's sound (วันศุกร์ = wan suk). And ๆ repeats the word before it (เร็วๆ = very fast).

characters.name_thai: ทัณฑฆาต (การันต์)
characters.sound_guide: Completely mutes the letter underneath it. Never pronounced.
characters.lookalike_warning: A small swirling flourish sitting above the silent letter.

characters.sound_guide: Repeats the preceding word to intensify it (e.g. เร็วๆ = very fast).
characters.lookalike_warning: Resembles the number 7 with a tail.

key_takeaways: Blends: two consonants typed back-to-back with no vowel (ปลา = bplaa).
The ์ (karan) mark makes the letter under it silent (วันศุกร์).
ๆ repeats the previous word to intensify it (ช้าๆ = slowly).
Blend letters are typed in order, with no space (ป + ล + า).
Look for ์ when a letter seems to disappear.

title: Blind Dictation & Fluent Touch Typing
subtitle: From Cognitive Reading to Subconscious Muscle Memory
summary: The final step: hear a Thai word, work out its sounds, class and vowels in your head, and type it without hints. This is the skill you have been building - now without the training wheels.

characters.sound_guide: Tapped 'r' sound. When used as a final consonant, pronounced as an 'n'!
characters.lookalike_warning: Heads inward and arcs upward to the right.

characters.sound_guide: Clear 'l' sound. When used as a final consonant, also pronounced as an 'n'!
characters.lookalike_warning: No tail on top (compare with ส).

key_takeaways: Hear -> identify the sounds -> check class and vowels -> type.
Final letters ร and ล can sound like 'n' (อาหาร = aa-haan).
Turn off guided hints in Keyboard Practice and test yourself.
Speed comes from repetition, not from thinking harder.
When you make a mistake, the app shows the key - use it to learn.
